title: Low-Calorie Dinner Recipes Under 400 Calories
description: These 8 satisfying low-calorie dinner recipes prove that healthy eating doesn't have to be boring. Each meal is under 400 calories and ready in 30 minutes.
author: Sarah Mitchell

content.text: One of the biggest myths about healthy eating is that low-calorie food is bland and unsatisfying. These eight recipes prove otherwise — each is packed with flavor, protein, and fiber to keep you full without busting your calorie budget.

items: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Zoodles — 285 calories, 28g protein
Turkey Taco Lettuce Wraps — 320 calories, 32g protein
Cauliflower Fried Rice with Egg — 290 calories, 14g protein
Baked Lemon Herb Salmon with Asparagus — 380 calories, 35g protein
Black Bean & Veggie Stuffed Peppers — 350 calories, 16g protein
Chicken & Broccoli Stir Fry (no rice) — 310 calories, 38g protein
Tomato Basil Zucchini Noodle Pasta — 260 calories, 12g protein
Spicy Thai Chicken Lettuce Cups — 295 calories, 30g protein

content.text: Preheat oven to 400°F. Place 2 salmon fillets on a lined baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil, squeeze half a lemon, and season with garlic powder, dill, salt, and pepper. Arrange asparagus spears alongside and roast for 12–15 minutes. The result is a restaurant-quality 380-calorie meal in under 20 minutes.
Swap white rice and pasta for zucchini noodles or cauliflower rice to cut 200+ calories from your dinner without feeling deprived.

Keeping dinners under 400 calories leaves room for a filling breakfast and lunch while staying within a 1400–1600 calorie daily target suitable for most women seeking moderate weight loss. Men can add a side salad or extra protein to scale up to 500 calories.

items.question: How do I make low-calorie meals more filling?
items.answer: Prioritize high-volume, low-calorie foods like leafy greens, cucumbers, and broth-based soups. Add lean protein (chicken, shrimp, tofu) to every meal and include fiber from vegetables and legumes.

items.question: Can I meal prep low-calorie dinners?
items.answer: Yes. Most of these recipes store well in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cook proteins in bulk on Sunday and pair them with different veggie sides throughout the week.
